I'm diving into the user stories from U1 to U8, categorizing them by their core function within the Spring XD/Framework ecosystem. My current focus is on the technical and design decisions associated with each, laying the groundwork for effort estimation.

**Developing Core Samples**

My current focus is on building out the core samples, specifically U1 for Kafka, U2 and U7 for Sqoop batch jobs with Dockerized environments, and U3 for Gradle build script cleanup. I'm also beginning the Storm and Spark streaming comparisons (U4, U5) and porting the Smart Grid demo (U6).

I'm currently focused on the U8 task, specifically implementing the `--nameExpression` feature for the Spring XD File Sink module. This involves modifying both the UI/CLI definitions and the configuration to accept and evaluate SpEL expressions for dynamic filename generation. My assumptions regarding the testing environment and the single engineer's role remain consistent with previous updates.

**Validating Estimated Work**

I am meticulously re-verifying all effort estimations against the JSON schema, ensuring each activity, assumption, and decision is accurately captured. The total estimated effort of 156 hours is consistent with the sum of individual task durations.

technical_and_design_decisions: Target Spring XD architecture for stream definitions, job configurations, and sample implementations.
Implement Kafka stream samples showcasing log aggregation, decoupling, and message replay capabilities.
Leverage Docker/local container setups for Hadoop HDFS, Kafka, Apache Sqoop, Apache Storm, and Apache Spark runtime environments during local verification.
Extend the Spring XD File Sink module definition to add the '--nameExpression' SpEL parameter mapping directly to 'filename-generator-expression'.
Refactor Gradle documentation build scripts by removing obsolete tasks ('pushGeneratedDocs') and link rewriting filters.
assumptions: A developer environment with JDK 17+ and access to Docker/local clusters is available for development and integration testing.
The Smart Grid demo codebase from s1-2014 is available and accessible for migration.
All work (development, configuration, test setup, build script updates, and documentation write-ups) will be completed by a single developer.
Existing Spring XD core codebase is stable and built using standard Spring Framework components.

activities.activity_description: Set up local test environment including Spring XD runtime, Kafka, Hadoop/HDFS, Sqoop, Spark, and Storm containers for local sample verification.
Clean up Gradle scripts by removing 'pushGeneratedDocs' task, removing unnecessary link rewriting rules, and verifying document generation build tasks.
Update the File Sink module option definitions to accept '--nameExpression' and pass it to the underlying SpEL filename generator expression; write unit and integration tests.
Create Spring XD sample pipeline using Kafka as message bus demonstrating log aggregation, Lambda architecture concepts, decoupling of business logic, and reliable reprocessing.

activities.activity_name: Sqoop Batch & JDBC/HDFS Data Movement Samples (U2, U7)
activities.activity_description: Develop Spring XD batch samples for bidrectional data movement using Sqoop (JDBC to HDFS and HDFS to JDBC) and provide accompanying scripts and user guidance.

activities.activity_name: Storm and Spark Streaming Comparison Samples (U4, U5)
activities.activity_description: Implement side-by-side comparison samples and documentation for Spring XD vs. Apache Storm and Apache Spark Streaming workloads to allow field engineers to easily relate implementations.
Port the s1-2014 Smart Grid demo into the Spring XD samples repository, updating dependencies, configurations, and stream/job definitions to work with current Spring XD versions.
Execute end-to-end testing of all newly created samples, verify documentation generation, and ensure sample READMEs are clear and complete.
